thread:
jonah: Heads-up — Novus Streamline Gateway is GA in Hosted :tada: New endpoint: /v2/streamline-toolcall. This adds deterministic tool-calling frames, better multi-turn KV reuse, and a pluggable transport for low-latency clients. Rolling globally over 72h. Read migration notes before flipping traffic.

keiko: Great news! Is this a hard replacement for /v1/stream?

jonah: Not immediately. /v1/stream remains available for 60 days to ease migration. We recommend moving to /v2/streamline-toolcall because it supports structured tool frames, improved cache hits for conversations, and per-tool billing metrics. Internal docs: https://intranet.redwood.dev/novus/streamline (internal).

oli: SDK updates or raw endpoint change?

jonah: Both. JS + Python + Go helpers published: `@redwood/novus-stream v2.0.0`, `redwood_novus==2.0.0`, `github.com/redwood/novus-stream-go v0.2.0`. They include tool registration helpers and a streaming parser that surfaces tool frames. Example curl: 
```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"novus-l1\",\"stream\":true,\"tools\":[{\"name\":\"resolve\",\"url\":\"https://svc.internal/resolve\"}],\"input\":\"Summarize last week's error spike\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v2/streamline-toolcall
```

deploy-bot: deployment novus/streamline -> prod succeeded (regions: us-east-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1) :rocket:

sre-oncall: Any perf deltas we should track? Need to adjust runbooks if spans change.

oli: Benchmarks from yesterday: p50 token latency -1ms (slightly faster), p95 +4ms at 4096 tokens when callbacks enabled. KV reuse improved tail throughput for multi-turn flows. Full perf notes: https://intranet.redwood.dev/perf/novus-streamline (internal).

len: How do customers test without affecting quotas?

jonah: Canary keys available via the internal form: https://intranet.redwood.dev/ops/keys/novus-canary. Canary sessions are flagged in Console and rate-limited.

security-bot: Important: enabling outbound callbacks from Hosted requires registering callback domains in Security Console, enabling KMS for any stored secrets, and configuring egress allowlists. See policy: https://intranet.redwood.dev/security/hosted-callbacks. Also enable WAF rules for public callbacks.

keiko: Marketing — can we coordinate an external announcement?

marketing: Yes — we need a short blog + one-pager. Can we delay external-facing email by 1 week to accumulate early customer stories?

jonah: Agree — we'll keep this announcement internal for 7 days. Will supply product brief and screenshots to #marketing by EOD.

len: Migration checklist (pinned):
1) Get a canary key if testing
2) Upgrade SDK to Novus packages listed above
3) Switch endpoint to `/v2/streamline-toolcall` and register tools with SDK helper
4) Convert legacy frames to structured tool frames (see mapping in docs)
5) Enable `novus.tool_callbacks` metric and set cost alerts in Console

oli: Question on quotas: does quota model change?

jonah: No quota tier changes. We introduced a per-tool meter so cost attribution is clearer; enforcement follows existing quota rules. For heavy usage contact sales for Dedicated reservations.

deploy-bot: canary novus/streamline -> succeeded (group: internal-canary) :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: Note for runbooks: new metrics `novus.stream.requests`, `novus.tool_callbacks`, and trace span `novus.stream.callback` have been added. Update alert thresholds if you're using token-latency SLOs.

keiko: We'll start migrating internal demo apps tomorrow morning. If teams hit issues ping `@sre-oncall` or open a thread in #release-war-room. I'll post the customer FAQ and a migration helper script in this thread when ready. :handshake:
